pairs.subject: settings
pairs.evidence: playwright.config.ts:6 The operational port setting is converted without checking finiteness, integrality, or port range, allowing malformed configuration to reach both the test URL and server command.

techniques.evidence: next.config.ts:84 This collection is declared in source, rather than seeded into a collection users can individually edit or delete.
next.config.ts:142 The configuration uses a programmatic wrapper; the inspected configs do not declare parent configuration documents or an include graph.
next.config.ts:7 This reads package metadata without an application save path that overwrites an operator-owned settings file.
next.config.ts:77 One environment source supplies this value, with a constant default; no independently supplied configuration sources are composed.
next.config.ts:135 This combines source-defined build rules, rather than round-tripping a durable user settings document or reloading an observed settings object.
next.config.ts:130 The environment controls configuration evaluation; there is no persisted override following a continuously changing upstream preference.
next.config.ts:78 The inspected setting has one input spelling and no deprecated alias competing during a rename grace period.
playwright.config.ts:28 The consumer uses an already evaluated in-memory configuration value; there is no per-key settings-storage round trip to batch.
playwright.config.ts:6 Number conversion accepts NaN, fractional numbers, and out-of-range ports without validation; the result is reused in baseURL and the webServer configuration.
